newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Euro MPs attack Fischler over Irish beef penalty cut.
newsitem.headline: Euro MPs attack Fischler over Irish beef penalty cut.

text.p: An inspection team to Ireland to check controls on beef stores which led to a fifty percent cut in penalties is still in place, Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler told the European Parliament on Monday.

Angry MEPs demanded to know why the European Commission had cut from 116 million Ecus to 62 million Ecus fines imposed on the Irish authorities for not applying proper controls on beef held in intervention stores.

"There seems to have been a bloody great fiddle in which people have got the money which your directorate general and your financial control did not think they should have," British Labour MEP John Tomlinson told Fischler.
Ireland had its fines reduced after telling a conciliation procedure that it had taken measures to imporve its controls, Fischler told the European Parliament's budgetary control committee.
"The Commission looked at the arbitration report which said that the reduction would be justified," he told the committee.
Since then there had been no possibility of verifying the controls since beef intervention had been suspended, he said.
"There was no intervention for three years until the BSE crisis and the Commission felt that it could not penalise Ireland for a situation that it had no control over, he added.
Since June, Irish inspectors had been on a strike which only ended last week and an EU inspection visit will now be made, Fischler said.
